## Running Dev Servers with portless

[portless](https://www.npmjs.com/package/portless) gives every dev server a stable, named `.localhost` HTTPS URL instead of a port number. **Agents should always start dev servers with `portless` rather than `npm run dev`**, because multiple agents/worktrees frequently run at once and hardcoded ports collide.

This repo is already configured — `package.json` declares the portless app name and the script to run, so no arguments are needed:

```bash
portless                 # starts the dev server, prints its URL
portless list            # show active routes and their URLs
portless get <name>      # print the URL for a named service
portless doctor          # diagnose proxy / DNS / CA trust issues
portless prune           # kill orphaned dev servers from crashed sessions
```

### Why this matters for worktrees

When run inside a git worktree, portless derives a per-worktree subdomain (`https://<worktree>.<app>.localhost`). That means:

- No port conflicts between worktrees or parallel agent sessions.
- Each worktree gets its own origin, so cookies/localStorage don't clash across branches.
- URLs are stable and derivable from the worktree name, so an agent can reason about them without scraping server logs.

Never assume `localhost:4000`. Resolve the actual URL with `portless list` / `portless get <name>`, or read the URL portless prints on startup.

### Notes

- The Vite config honours the `PORT` env var (with `strictPort`) so portless can assign the port; don't reintroduce a hardcoded port.
- Playwright still runs against its own configured base URL — use portless for interactive/manual dev servers, not to override the test config.
- If a URL doesn't resolve, run `portless doctor` first (common fixes: `portless trust`, `portless hosts sync`)."},{"filePath":"/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care_fe/docs/local-development.md","oldString":"## Build/Lint Commands

portless - Replace port numbers with stable, named .localhost URLs. For humans and agents.

Eliminates port conflicts, memorizing port numbers, and cookie/storage
clashes by giving each dev server a stable .localhost URL.

Install:
  npm install -g portless          Global (recommended)
  npm install -D portless          Project dev dependency

Requirements:
  Node.js 24+

Usage:
  portless                         Run dev script through proxy
  portless                         From monorepo root: run all workspace packages
  portless run                     Same as above
  portless run <cmd>               Run a command through the proxy
  portless <name> <cmd>            Run with an explicit app name
  portless proxy start             Start the proxy (HTTPS on port 443, daemon); rarely needed since it auto-starts on first run
  portless proxy stop              Stop the proxy
  portless service install         Start proxy automatically when the OS starts
  portless get <name>              Print URL for a service (for cross-service refs)
  portless alias <name> <port>     Register a static route (e.g. for Docker)
  portless alias --remove <name>   Remove a static route
  portless list                    Show active routes
  portless doctor                  Check local portless health
  portless trust                   Add local CA to system trust store
  portless clean                   Remove portless state, trust entry, and hosts block
  portless prune                   Kill orphaned dev servers from crashed sessions
  portless hosts sync              Add routes to /etc/hosts (fixes Safari)
  portless hosts clean             Remove portless entries from /etc/hosts

Examples:
  portless                            # Run dev script through proxy
  portless                            # From monorepo root: start all apps
  portless --script start             # Run "start" script instead of "dev"
  portless myapp next dev             # -> https://myapp.localhost
  portless run next dev               # -> https://<project>.localhost
  portless run next dev               # in worktree -> https://<worktree>.<project>.localhost
  portless service install            # Start HTTPS proxy on OS startup
  portless service install --lan      # Persist LAN mode in the startup service
  portless service install --wildcard # Persist wildcard routing in the startup service
  portless get backend                # -> https://backend.localhost
  portless doctor                     # Check proxy, routes, DNS, and CA trust
  portless myapp --tailscale next dev # -> also https://<node>.ts.net (tailnet)
  portless myapp --funnel next dev    # -> also https://<node>.ts.net (public)
  portless myapp --ngrok next dev     # -> also https://<random>.ngrok.app (public)

Configuration (portless.json):
  Optional. Portless works out of the box by running the "dev" script
  from package.json. Use portless.json to override defaults.

  Override name:   { "name": "myapp" }
  Override script: { "name": "myapp", "script": "start" }
  Monorepo:        { "apps": { "apps/web": { "name": "myapp" } } }

- `portless` — **Preferred** way to start the dev server (see [Dev Servers](#dev-servers-portless))
- `npm run dev` — Start dev server directly at http://localhost:4000 (only if portless is unavailable)
- `npm run build` — Production build (takes 2+ minutes, set timeout to 180s+)
- `npm run lint` — Run ESLint (takes 85s+, set timeout to 120s+)
- `npm run lint-fix` — ESLint with auto-fix
- `npm run format` — Prettier formatting

See [`docs/local-development.md`](docs/local-development.md) for the full local setup and [`docs/testing.md`](docs/testing.md) for E2E testing.

## Dev Servers (portless)

Agents should start dev servers with [`portless`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/portless) instead of `npm run dev`. It proxies each dev server behind a stable `https://<name>.localhost` URL, so parallel agents and git worktrees never fight over a fixed port.

```bash
portless           # runs the configured script; prints the URL it is served on
```

Why this matters for autonomous work:

- **No port conflicts.** portless assigns a free port and injects it as `PORT`; `vite.config.mts` honours `PORT` with `strictPort`, so multiple checkouts can run at once.
- **Worktree isolation.** From a git worktree the URL is namespaced per worktree, so each branch gets its own origin — and its own cookies/localStorage, avoiding cross-branch auth/session bleed.
- **Stable URLs.** The URL is derived from config, not from whichever port happened to be free, so it can be reused across restarts in browser tooling and tests.

Useful commands:

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `portless` | Start the dev server through the proxy |
| `portless list` | Show active routes and their URLs |
| `portless get <name>` | Print the URL for a running service |
| `portless doctor` | Diagnose proxy, DNS, and CA-trust issues |
| `portless prune` | Kill orphaned dev servers left by crashed sessions |

Notes:

- The app name and script live under the `portless` key in [`package.json`](package.json) — read it there rather than assuming a URL. Prefer `portless get <name>` / `portless list` to resolve the live URL.
- Run `portless` as a long-lived background process and keep it running; do not restart it for every change (Vite HMR handles updates).
- The proxy serves HTTPS with a locally generated CA. Browser tooling works once `portless trust` has been run; for `curl`, pass `--cacert ~/.portless/ca.pem`.
- If portless is not installed, fall back to `npm run dev` (or `PORT=<port> npm run dev` when you need a specific port)."}]}
